answer: Admission runs through a narrow canyon: each new key must solve a cipher-bound sequential puzzle that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelised, proving one operator behind one key. At the jetty, an established agent posts a refundable deposit for the newcomer, forfeited if the identity is exposed as fake within three epochs. A farm must pay the time cost and a deposit per fake, while sponsors refuse to vouch for identities they cannot verify, so mass creation becomes slow, expensive, and self-limiting.
